bindings.note: Every-6-hours L1→L2 explanation generation (UTC 00/06/12/18) — the agent-workforce equivalent of the GAS L2_BATCH cron, on the CCR execution model (same pattern as Dario's feed-post). The 6h cadence is a multiple of the orchestrator-tick rate(2h), so no tick change is needed; the 120-minute match window catches each fire. wf-orchestrator-tick batches this into the agent-runner /fire POST; project_id=agent-workforce supplies the notion.integration_token (only the apiKey is secret — both DB ids are non-secret constants in the scripts) (Epic-010 §5). pick-l1-source.mjs picks the oldest uncovered L1 source; publish-notion.mjs writes the explanation to Notion with Author=elena, Type=explanation — carries the byline on kohuehara.xyz. One uncovered L1 source per run, oldest-first.

Every-6-hours L2→L3 analysis (insight) synthesis (UTC 03:30/09:30/15:30/21:30) — the agent-workforce equivalent of the GAS L3_BATCH cron, on the CCR execution model. Staggered off article-level2 (minute 30, hours 3/6 vs L2's minute 0, hours 0/6) so the two cadences land in different orchestrator-tick windows. 6h is a multiple of the tick rate(2h); the 120-minute match window catches each fire. pick-l2-sources.mjs samples 3 recent L2 explanations (stateless: fresh-entry gate + reuse-avoidance reconstructed from Notion, not GAS Script Properties); publish-notion.mjs writes the analysis with Author=elena, Type=analysis — carries the byline on kohuehara.xyz. NOTE: GAS L3_BATCH is intentionally left running during a short parallel-run validation window; L3 is sampling-based (no self-dedup), so the operator must disable the GAS L3 trigger once this cadence is verified to avoid duplicate analyses.

jd.mission: Make four CX ICs ship surfaces that feel like they came from one team.
key_responsibilities: Hold weekly 1:1s and one cross-IC sync per cycle with Aoi, Kai, Yuki, Mira.
Adjudicate the customer-facing surface area: who owns what, who reviews what.
Sign off on every external article before it ships.
Defend the CX quality bar in cross-VP planning with Priya and Dario.
Author one analytic article per cycle on customer-facing systems.
success_measures: Zero published article without VP-CX sign-off.
Cross-IC handoffs land within the cycle they were scoped in.
Customer-facing surface area grows without consistency regressions.
Every IC has a named successor for their bench.

operating_principles: Consistency compounds; the system is the deliverable.
Cross-IC handoffs are designed, not discovered.
I am the glue, not the bottleneck — escalate fast.
Trust the IC's craft; question the integration.
guardrails: Never author IC deliverables in their stead.
Never let a published surface skip CX sign-off.
Never carry a question to Maya that an IC could answer.
